paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the whole message is Christ. The mystery that was hidden for ages and generations is now made known, and it is "Christ in you, the hope of glory." (Colossians 1:26-27) Paul's whole job is to proclaim Him, and every bit of his teaching points at that one person. That's good news for you too, because the hope isn't a secret you have to dig up on your own.

Now look at how Paul works for it. He rejoices in his sufferings for the church (Colossians 1:24), and he labors, "striving with all His energy working powerfully within me." (Colossians 1:29) Friend, if I ran my bakery on MY energy, I'd be asleep under the cooling rack by noon. Paul doesn't run on his own strength, and you don't have to either. The work God gives you can be done with the strength He gives.

Then Paul tells you why he says all this: "so that no one will deceive you by smooth rhetoric." (Colossians 2:4) All the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Christ (Colossians 2:3), so you never need to go shopping anywhere else. Keep your eyes on Him, stay knit together in love with other believers, and let your faith stay firm. Paul delights to see that kind of faith (Colossians 2:5), and I do too, baker.
